To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in an acute lung injury (AL) setting, the use of Omegavean or Clinoleic is more effective than the use of intralipid in reducing the intensity of cytokine storm and cell apoptosis caused by L-PS challenge, and that Omegaven in particular is able to improve liver function.
preconditioning with Omegan or Clinoleic prior to acute lung induced by LPS is superior to Intralipids.

the use of Omegavan and Clinoleic lipid emulsion, particularly in patients ALI, is characterized by uncertainty due the lack of relevant studies, and that future investigations should specifically focus on the mode of application (bolus vs. continuous) and determining the best timepoint for administration.

the use of Omegavan or Clinoleic for patients with ALIs.
the effect of lipid emulsification on the production of proinflammatory factors and apoptosis in rats with ALI.
the effects of three representative lipid emulsions on the production of inflammatory mediates in the serum and the apoptosis of lung tissue in an ALI model.

fish oil-based lipid preconditioning is better than Intralypid in decreasing the cytokine storm, and Omegavan in addition has potential to improve liver functions in an ALI rat model.

the fish oil-based lipid preparation is better than the olive oil-based lipid preparation in decreasing the intensity and duration of the cytokine response, and that the olive oil-based preparation is better than Intralibid in decreasing the apoptosis in the lungs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipid emulsion preconditioning prior to LPS-induced ALI can alter the inflammatory and apoptotic responses in the lung and the liver.
lipid emulsion via intravenous route may be beneficial to ALI patients, but the effect may depend on the type of lipid emulsion used.
the lipid emulsion preconditioning could affect cytokine production and liver function in the lung and hepatic tissues in an ALI model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Omegavan or Clinoleic may be better than Intralipe for patients with ALIs, and the fish oil based lipid emulsion may be more suitable for the critically ill patients.

the fish oil-based lipid preparation (Clinoleic) or the fish oil-based intravenous lipid emulsion (Omegaven) is superior to a soy oil-based intravenous fat emulsion (Intralipid) in the setting of acute lung injury.

the fish oil-based lipid preparation, Omegaven, is superior to Intralipids in decreasing the intensity and duration of the cytokine release, and in reducing apoptosis of the lung tissue in ALI setting.
